*Written by the map agent (Opus 5.5, fresh; rules 6 and 7 of `S108 Part A - how the replies will be read, written before sending.md`), 28 September 2026. Built by `S108 Part A - computation/map/s108_map_build.py` from the frozen template, the frozen set, the tabulation, the four "variants computed" files and their edge `.json`, and the program's D18.1 graph after round 4 (its source read, not run); every input's md5 is in the `.json` (`inputs`). An experiment on copies (rule 11): nothing here changes the theory's text, formal core, claims or program, and nothing is ruled. "Candidate" or "explanation" for what the theory judges; "model" only for the program's own small structures (S43).*

Status: complete, 28 September 2026. The candidate list (rule 7) is `S108 Part A - candidate definitions of explanation.md`.

**Corrected by the second checker** (a fresh Opus 5.5 agent, rule 9; the orchestrator's decision 1), 28 September 2026, on the critical review's O1–O13: rebuilt by `S108 Part A - computation/map/s108_map_build_second_checker.py` (the builder above with each change marked). What changed and why: `S108 Part A - the second checker on the critical review.md`. Two results here are the second checker's runs, not a section's: the owner's weathervane and two-part sign with the change read as a boundary (O1, §2's V2.3 row) and V3.5 with a construction trace spanning occurrences (O3, e3.25c); their scripts and outputs are in `S108 Part A - computation/second checker/`. Nothing ruled; nothing applied to the theory (rule 11).

## 0. What the map holds, and how to read it

| | count |
|---|---|
| nodes | 859: 815 template items (688 sentences, 127 definitions and encodings; 238 FROZEN, 577 middle) + 10 parts of the explanation definition + 32 claims + 2 cases named by edges |
| variants | 32 tabulated; 29 run; 3 flagged and not run (V1.6, V1.7, V2.8) |
| source rows | 182 (the four `.json`); 18 split by standing; 4 'none found' rows kept apart (§4) |
| edges | 221 (21 summary edges): computed 179, claimed only 31, contradicted 11; blocks 21, constrains 33, changes with 79, moves 50, independent of 38 |
| template items touched | computed 142, claimed only 26, untouched 647 (middle untouched: 473 of 577) |

- **from**: the item or items the variant varies (definitions; the sentences varied with them are in the `.json`). **to**: the items the edge names: template ids (`L<line>.s|n<k>`, `D…`, `E…`), the parts of the explanation definition (`X:…`, §1), claims (`FC…`) and two cases.
- **Kinds**: *blocks* (under the variant the item is false or has no reading); *constrains* (the item limits the variant and stays readable); *changes with* (the item's extension or wording moves with the variant); *moves* (what the item holds of changes); *independent of* (computed: the item does not move; a negative edge, kept so that "no move" is not read from silence, rule 3).
- **Standing**: *computed* (a run shows it); *contradicted* (a run shows otherwise); *claimed only* (the reply's argument, or the computing agent's where marked, with what would settle it). "cond." = shown only under the reading named. A source row whose parts differ in standing is split (`e<s>.<row>a`, `b`, …). Rows whose content is "none found" are listed apart (§4). Summary edges (`s<n>`) carry a file's own summary table where no row gives the variant's effect on (E) or on being an explanation.

### What the computation shows about the dependencies of the explanation definition (short)

- **(E) moves only when its own reads move.** Of the 29 variants run, six move which candidates meet (E): V1.1 (D1.4, what (F1) reads), V2.1–V2.3 (D6.4, Dependence's witness), V2.4 (D6.7, (E) itself) and V1.5, whose reading adds a conjunct "p is a question" to (E) (S108-1-I5). Every other section-1 item varied (D2.1, D2.4, D2.6, D3.3) moves families, Prod or Ident and never (E) (0 of 61,914 generated candidates), as D18.1's graph has it (Roles and Respects are not upstream of (E)).
- **Being an explanation moves with Dec and with D16.XV's rule, not with (E).** With (E) unmoved: V2.5 (D12.1, Sel with H = ∅), V3.6 (D15.8, the population's parts clause; on S108-3-I4) and V4.1–V4.3 (D16.XV). V3.4 (D13.3's ExplUse) and V3.5 (D13.8's record clause) reach Dec only under a reading: D12.2 as written reads Prepares, not ExplUse (contradicted, e3.20a); and its Held(o′, x) at o′ ⪯ o_t makes the record clause idle for every candidate meeting (E) when the trace lies at o_t (0 of 115,400 chains, cut T′; e3.25a, e3.26), not when the trace spans an unrecorded change of contract (e3.25c, the second checker's run: every such held output moves).
- **D18.1's reach is needed, and not enough.** Every computed move of Acc or of Account ∧ ¬Dec(t) is of a variant whose node the graph places upstream of (E) or Dec, or of one whose reading adds that edge (V1.5: ρ_p into (E); V3.4 under S108-3-I2: ExplUse into CT). One reach carries no move for candidates meeting (E) in the program's encoding: V3.5 (Episode → Con → Dec), screened by Held at o_t when the trace lies at o_t (§2's last column); with a trace spanning an unrecorded change the reach carries (e3.25c).
- **What the owner's changes are read as.** V2.3 (a contrast needs an edit) keeps the owner's weathervane and two-part sign as the program encodes them (the wind and Tuesday as edits: M13, `claims_s106`) and drops both, with every candidate on their questions, when the change is read as a boundary (FC28.new2's D_vane; the sign with Monday and Tuesday as boundaries): the second checker's run, §2.
- **Ruling out, conflict, creation and universality are downstream or aside.** V3.1–V3.3 (D9.7, D9.4, D9.6) and V4.4 move who has ruled what out, problems and the (Suff)/(Nec) defeat sets, never (E) or being an explanation; V2.6, V2.7 (D8.2, D8.5) move rivalry and conflict with a claim; V3.7, V3.8 (D11.4, D14.7) move (P) attribution and (EX); V4.6–V4.8 move 𝔈_Θ, UU (a toy) and (Prov)(i). Each with 0 moves of Acc and of Account ∧ ¬Dec(t) (§2).
- **Where the frozen words hold the middle.** Computed blocks of FROZEN items: D4.4 (V1.1); L347.s2 (V1.2, V1.8); L307.s1 (V2.2); L315.s1, L317.s6 (V2.6); L403.s3 (V3.4); L375.s2 (V3.7); L495.s1 (V4.7, toy only); and L528.s2–s3 change with V3.8, D13.4 and D13.5 with V1.1 (V1.1 blocks the claim FC85 (a), 'a content matches itself', which D13.4 does not state). By the template's own rule a variant that blocks a FROZEN item is not a reading of the frozen words (§3). No flagged candidate of V2.3, V2.4, V2.5, V4.1, V4.2 blocks a FROZEN item: what they sit against is an owner's decision (the candidate list).
- **The replies' claims the computation contradicts: 11 edges** (§5); among them the replies' routes from D13.3 and D13.8 to Dec (the latter only where the trace lies at o_t), V2.3's block of L329.s3, V4.5's reach to E5, V4.3's "no record" case, and V2.2's "every candidate realizing L299.s1 fails (E)". V3.2's "fewer problems" is now a computed move with the reply's direction contradicted (problems grow; e3.09b).

If the wind and the day are read as changes made to the vane and the sign, as the program reads them, nothing changes. *Seems to go against*, on the first reading only, S41 Q15: "Yes, it can be explained", and S44: "In either case, it is an explanation."

**C6 (V2.4).** *In one sentence:* something whose answer is simply written into one of its parts fails the tests and is not an explanation at all, not even a bad one. *Example:* a table that just lists the answers would no longer be an explanation; nor would "the sign has one part that is red on Mondays and blue on Tuesdays" (not your case: a companion the program sets beside it). Your own case, a red part that switches on on Mondays and a blue part that switches on on Tuesdays, stays an explanation on the program's reading of "written in", under which a part counts as written in only if it alone gives the answer at every point asked about (each of your parts gives it on one day only). On the other readings, where giving the answer at some of the points is enough, your two-part explanation stops being one too. *Seems to go against* S45: "Yes, take the test out"; and, on those other readings only, S44: "In either case, it is an explanation."

**C7 (V2.5).** *In one sentence:* a link counts as picked out by trial even when nothing at all was tried, so a link someone simply writes down from nothing can be an explanation. *Example:* someone who has never watched a pendulum writes a formula on a napkin and says "this stands for the pendulum"; with nothing tried and nothing copied, under this reading it is an explanation. A student copying the same formula from a textbook still is not. *Seems to go against* S41 Q2: "No, not if just declared".

**C8 (V3.4).** *In one sentence:* a link someone worked out counts as worked out only if the explanation they leaned on while working it out itself passes the tests; if it does not, the link counts as merely declared. (Only under one reading of what "the construction" of a link is.) *Example:* a navigator works out a course with a method that does not hold for the open sea, and the course still comes out right for the harbour she was asked about; under this reading her course counts as merely declared, so it is not an explanation of the way to the harbour, although it passes every test there. *Seems to go against* S41 Q2, "No, not if just declared": the question you answered set a link simply declared against one found by trial or worked out, and her link was worked out.

**C11 (V4.1).** *In one sentence:* something whose answer is simply written into one of its parts can still pass the tests, but is not an explanation. *Example:* "it is red because it is red" passes the tests but would not count as an explanation; nor would "the sign has one part that is red on Mondays and blue on Tuesdays" (not your case: the program's companion to it). **C12 (V4.2).** *In one sentence:* anything that passes the tests is an explanation, even if its link to what it explains was only declared. *Example:* a student copies a pendulum formula that works and writes "this stands for the pendulum"; under this reading that is an explanation. *Seems to go against* S41 Q2: "No, not if just declared".

113	        """D^R (D8.1): the relations at the one pair (a, b) replaced by R (comp -> relation)."""
114	        o = self._copy()
115	        o.override = dict(self.override)
116	        for j, rel in R.items():
117	            o.override[(j, a, b)] = frozenset(rel)

120	    # relations ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
121	    def full(self, j):
122	        if j not in self._full:
123	            self._full[j] = frozenset(itertools.product(*[self.dom[v] for v in self.foot[j]]))
124	        return self._full[j]

126	    def L(self, j, a, b):
127	        if j in self.deleted:
128	            return self.full(j)
129	        if (j, a, b) in self.override:
130	            return self.override[(j, a, b)]
131	        return frozenset(self._L(j, a, b))

133	    def compose(self, a2, a1):
134	        """a2·a1 (partial). The identity law is built in (D1.1)."""
135	        if a1 == ONE:
136	            return a2
137	        if a2 == ONE:
138	            return a1
139	        return self._compose(a2, a1)

141	    # solutions ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
142	    def sol(self, a, b):
143	        """Sol_D(a, b) (O), as tuples over self.ports."""
144	        key = ("sol", a, b)
145	        if key not in self._cache:
146	            cons = [(self.foot[j], self.L(j, a, b)) for j in self.comps]
147	            self._cache[key] = frozenset(solve(self.ports, self.dom, cons))
148	        return self._cache[key]

150	    def ports_of(self, N):
151	        vs = []
152	        for j in self.comps:
153	            if j in N:
154	                for v in self.foot[j]:
155	                    if v not in vs:
156	                        vs.append(v)
157	        return tuple(v for v in self.ports if v in vs)

159	    def sol_sub(self, N, a, b):
160	        """Sol_N(a, b) (D1.4, I14): the constraints of N alone, over V_N (ordered as self.ports)."""
161	        N = frozenset(N)
162	        key = ("sub", N, a, b)
163	        if key not in self._cache:
164	            # Area 2 [A2-04, amends I14]: the whole target as a subnetwork keeps every port of D,
165	            # a port in no footprint included, so Sol_{J_D} = Sol_D (FC25 (b)).
166	            VN = self.ports if N >= frozenset(self.comps) else self.ports_of(N)
167	            cons = [(self.foot[j], self.L(j, a, b)) for j in self.comps if j in N]
168	            self._cache[key] = (VN, frozenset(solve(VN, self.dom, cons)))
169	        return self._cache[key]

171	    def proj(self, sols, ports, onto):
172	        idx = [ports.index(p) for p in onto]
173	        return frozenset(tuple(z[i] for i in idx) for z in sols)

184	        comp_tab = []

216	def sets_through(org, a, b, v, j):
217	    """a sets port v through component j at b (D2.1, I04)."""
218	    if v not in org.foot[j]:
219	        return False
220	    rel = org.L(j, a, b)
221	    i = org.foot[j].index(v)
222	    xs = set(w[i] for w in rel)
223	    if len(xs) != 1:
224	        return False
225	    x = next(iter(xs))
226	    if rel != slice_rel(org, j, v, x):

229	        if k != j and org.L(k, a, b) != org.L(k, ONE, b):

240	class Roles:
241	    """Set_v, asg, Input, Output, Obs under both readings, families (D2.1-D2.4, D4.5-D4.6).
242	    exclude_identity: I80. Area 1 fix: default True (D2.1: a setting edit is an edit other than 1;
243	    L103 'replaces', L141 baseline, T13). Pass False for the round-2 literal reading."""
244	
245	    def __init__(self, org, exclude_identity=True):
246	        self.org = org
247	        self.exclude_identity = exclude_identity
248	        self.Set = {}
249	        self.through = {}
250	        for v in org.ports:
251	            S, T = [], set()
252	            for a in org.A:
253	                if exclude_identity and a == ONE:
254	                    continue
255	                ok = True
256	                js_a = set()
257	                for b in org.B:
258	                    js = [j for j in org.comps if sets_through(org, a, b, v, j)]
259	                    if not js:
260	                        ok = False
261	                        break
262	                    js_a.update(js)
263	                if ok:
264	                    S.append(a)
265	                    T.update(js_a)
266	            self.Set[v] = frozenset(S)
267	            self.through[v] = T
268	        # asg(v): the one component the setting edits of v set it through; undefined otherwise (I04)
269	        self.asg = {v: next(iter(self.through[v])) for v in org.ports if len(self.through[v]) == 1}
270	        self.alt = {j: frozenset(a for a in org.A if any(org.L(j, a, b) != org.L(j, ONE, b) for b in org.B)) for j in org.comps}
271	        # Slc_j (area 1, D2.6 new, A1-04): the edits that alter j and, at every b where they alter it, replace
272	        # it by a slice on a port j assigns: interventions on j, single or composite, whatever else they
273	        # alter. L57 sets them apart from edits to j's rule (H01).
274	        self.slc = {j: frozenset(a for a in self.alt[j] if self._slices(j, a)) for j in org.comps}
275	
276	    def _slices(self, j, a):
277	        org = self.org
278	        for b in org.B:
279	            rel = org.L(j, a, b)
280	            if rel == org.L(j, ONE, b):
281	                continue
282	            ok = False
283	            for i, v in enumerate(org.foot[j]):
284	                if self.asg.get(v) != j:
285	                    continue
286	                xs = set(w[i] for w in rel)
287	                if len(xs) == 1 and rel == slice_rel(org, j, v, next(iter(xs))):
288	                    ok = True
289	                    break
290	            if not ok:
291	                return False
292	        return True
293	
294	    def input(self, v):
295	        return bool(self.Set[v])
296	
297	    def output(self, v, j):
298	        """Out(v, j) (D2.3, I05): at the identity edit, at most one value of v given the others."""
299	        org = self.org
300	        if v not in org.foot[j]:
301	            return False
302	        i = org.foot[j].index(v)
303	        for b in org.B:
304	            seen = {}
305	            for w in org.L(j, ONE, b):
306	                key = w[:i] + w[i + 1:]
307	                if key in seen and seen[key] != w[i]:
308	                    return False
309	                seen[key] = w[i]
310	        return True
311	
312	    def outputs_of(self, j):
313	        """o_j: the ports j assigns. Where j assigns several, Set_{o_j} is the union [I102]."""
314	        return [v for v, k in self.asg.items() if k == j]
315	
316	    def set_oj(self, j):
317	        s = set()
318	        for v in self.outputs_of(j):
319	            s |= self.Set[v]
320	        return frozenset(s)
321	
322	    def obs(self, reading):
323	        """Obs (D2.4) under reading 'R-i' or 'R-ii' (I06). An (o, m) with asg(m) undefined yields no
324	        observation edits [I102]."""
325	        org = self.org
326	        out = set()
327	        for o, j in self.asg.items():
328	            for m in org.foot[j]:
329	                if m == o or m not in self.asg:
330	                    continue
331	                jm = self.asg[m]
332	                for a in org.A:
333	                    if a not in self.alt[j]:
334	                        continue
335	                    if any(org.L(jm, a, b) != org.L(jm, ONE, b) for b in org.B):
336	                        continue
337	                    if reading == "R-ii" and (a in self.Set[o] or a in self.slc[j]):
338	                        continue
339	                    out.add(a)
340	        return frozenset(out)
341	
342	    def obs_pairs(self, reading):
343	        org = self.org
344	        res = {}
345	        for o, j in self.asg.items():
346	            for m in org.foot[j]:
347	                if m == o or m not in self.asg:
348	                    continue
349	                jm = self.asg[m]
350	                s = set()
351	                for a in org.A:
352	                    if a in self.alt[j] and all(org.L(jm, a, b) == org.L(jm, ONE, b) for b in org.B):
353	                        if reading == "R-ii" and (a in self.Set[o] or a in self.slc[j]):
354	                            continue
355	                        s.add(a)
356	                res[(o, m)] = frozenset(s)
357	        return res

359	    # change and invariance on a contract (D4.5, I09) ------------------------------------------
360	    def changes(self, j, X, C):
361	        org = self.org
362	        return any(a in X and org.L(j, a, b) != org.L(j, ONE, b) for (a, b) in C)
363	
364	    def inv(self, j, X, C):
365	        org = self.org
366	        return all(org.L(j, a, b) == org.L(j, ONE, b) for (a, b) in C if a in X)
367	
368	    # families (D4.6) ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
369	    def causal(self, j, C, reading):
370	        return self.changes(j, self.set_oj(j), C) and self.inv(j, self.obs(reading), C)
371	
372	    def meas(self, j, m, C, reading):
373	        org = self.org
374	        if m not in org.foot[j] or m not in self.asg or self.asg.get(m) == j:  # area 1: asg(m) defined (U5)
375	            return False
376	        MR = self.alt[j] if reading == "R-i" else self.alt[j] - self.set_oj(j) - self.slc[j]
377	        return self.inv(j, self.Set[m], C) and self.changes(j, MR, C)
378	
379	    def world(self, j):
380	        s = set()
381	        for v in self.org.ports:
382	            if self.asg.get(v) != j:  # includes ports with asg undefined [I102]
383	                s |= self.Set[v]
384	        return frozenset(s)
385	
386	    def rule(self, j, C):
387	        # area 1: an edit to the rule is an edit that alters j and is no (single or composite) setting (H01, L57)
388	        return self.inv(j, self.world(j), C) and self.changes(j, self.alt[j] - self.set_oj(j) - self.slc[j], C)
389	
390	    def upstream(self, v, w):
391	        """v ⇝ w (D3.3 as fixed in area 1): components j_1..j_n and ports u_1..u_n with v ∈ V_{j_1} ∖ {u_1},
392	        Out(u_i, j_i) for every i ≤ n, u_i ∈ V_{j_{i+1}} ∖ {u_{i+1}} for i < n, and u_n = w."""
393	        org = self.org
394	        # frontier of (port u reached as an output of some component, having entered from a port ≠ u)
395	        start = set()
396	        for j in org.comps:
397	            if v in org.foot[j]:
398	                for u in org.foot[j]:
399	                    if u != v and self.output(u, j):
400	                        start.add(u)
401	        seen, todo = set(start), list(start)
402	        while todo:
403	            u = todo.pop()
404	            for j in org.comps:
405	                if u in org.foot[j]:
406	                    for u2 in org.foot[j]:
407	                        if u2 != u and u2 not in seen and self.output(u2, j):
408	                            seen.add(u2)
409	                            todo.append(u2)
410	        return w in seen
411	
412	    def families(self, C, reading):
413	        org = self.org
414	        return {
415	            "causal": sorted(j for j in org.comps if self.causal(j, C, reading)),
416	            "meas": sorted((j, m) for j in org.comps for m in org.foot[j] if self.meas(j, m, C, reading)),
417	            "rule": sorted(j for j in org.comps if self.rule(j, C)),
418	        }
